summary: Text-only round. R13-R18 genuinely closed, all three merges verified clean by set difference. What blocks: ADR-019 section 2 again ships a sentence its own committed evidence falsifies, and a deliberate suite-tagging deviation is justified by a ledger row that is in the wrong suite.

R13.evidence: Whole-suite in-process ablation at 178 cases: committed rule -> []; ss exclusion dropped -> ['resolver-narrows-singular-noun-ending-in-s']; widened back to [^\Wsui]s -> ['resolver-refuses-plural-menus']. Exactly one case each, neither direction tradeable. Regex probe over 44 phrasings: every regularly-inflected plural caught (menus, taxis, skis, gurus, addresses, classes, buses, analyses); over-firing residue exactly as declared. Honest, not a flattering subset.

R14.evidence: invariant, fast, invariant, fast, fast on HEAD: 64/64 (14.45s), 178/178 (73.12s), 64/64 (14.58s), 178/178 (72.75s), 178/178 (72.72s). Zero FAIL lines in all five; both band cases PASS in each. No green run reddens the next. Published 74.19s IS the ledger maximum at 178 and rule holds to 78.26s — 4.07s headroom against an observed 2.15s spread.

R15.evidence: The false universal is gone from all four sites; grep returns only the review record.

R16.evidence: Arithmetic replaced by a table of every deleted row. Table 1 re-derived against git show 820d807 -- evals/report/history.jsonl: five rows, all ts/suite/passed-total/wall_s match to the digit. No commit in e949f59..HEAD removes any ledger row.

R18.evidence: _nearest(page, loc, near, *, loose: bool); both call sites pass explicitly; _check_narrowing_fails_closed requires KEYWORD_ONLY AND default is empty, so restoring either a default or a positional kind is red. The PLACEMENT rationale is not sound.

merges.verdict: CLEAN, verified by set difference against both parents
merges.ledger: e101a38 1271+1444 -> 1496; 8c54d58 1541+1501 -> 1573; 62ed038 1585+1584 -> 1668 (1688 at HEAD). Zero rows lost from either parent in all three; nothing present that is in neither parent nor the merge's own gate runs.
merges.renames: evals/report/ 283+255 -> 301, zero missing either way at 62ed038; whole tree 712+672 -> 740 with exactly one missing (their own git mv of the ADR). e101a38's one apparent loss is NOT rename detection — origin/main deleted that report in 9840e23 (T-R44) and the three-way merge correctly took the deletion.
merges.adr: 026 collides with nothing on disk, origin/main (max 024) or any live ref (023 = M39, 025 = T-M40-5). Every live citation moved; tasks/reviews/ and evals/report/ correctly keep old numbers.
merges.opt_in_keys: per-key union verified across all three merges — no key dropped, no case-id dropped, nothing added that was in neither parent.
merges.item_10: used, not worked around: ADR-019:94-96 carries both restatements in the marked form and both match their bullets.

findings.claim: ADR-019 section 2's band bullet states the row it cites has two red cases; that row is 178/178 with zero failures — the two reds belong to 20260824-024553, the row cited before the merge re-citation, and the sentence was left behind.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:68-73. Line 68 (62ed038) publishes ts 20260824-024916, 74.19s, 178/178; lines 71-73 (8c54d58, one merge earlier) say 'Its two reds are docs-numbers-are-derived and published-band-matches-the-ledger'. The ledger row is 178/178 and the report's failed set is empty. Those two reds are 20260824-024553's (73.47s, 176/178). Nothing goes red: item 2 grades only the stated passed/total, and item 10 grades only sentences in the marked restated form, which this one is not.
findings.acceptance: The parenthetical describes the row it cites, or names 20260824-024553 explicitly as the superseded citation. No sentence in the bullet contradicts the 178/178 three lines above it.

findings.claim: The stated reason resolver-narrowing-fails-closed is kept out of the invariant suite is false: the cited '59-case invariant row from 2026-08-16 (32.25s)' is a FAST row, and _band_wrong filters by suite as well as count, so it can never enter an invariant band.
findings.evidence: resolver-narrowing-fails-closed.json:20 why_not_invariant. The only 32.25s row is history.jsonl:15, suite 'fast', total 59. eval_adapter.py:620-621 filters r['suite'] == suite and r['total'] == now. T-R53 states the same in prose. The 41 invariant rows at 59 cases all run 13.09-14.80s and derive 20. The claim is also stale by count: invariant is 64 post-merge, so adding this makes 65, not 59. Net effect: an L1 pure-code check the case file itself calls 'invariant by shape' sits outside the 100%-gated suite on a justification the committed ledger falsifies, repeated in 92cee87's commit message.
findings.acceptance: Either the case moves to invariant (and the band is republished at 65 with the receipt commit that always costs), or why_not_invariant states the real obstacle and stops describing a fast row as an invariant one.

findings.claim: The merges orphaned half a sentence in ADR-019 section 2: its head moved up to the graded restatement block and its tail was left dangling at the end of the ablation-deletion paragraph, where it now reads as a claim about T-M38-5.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:176-180. At the review baseline the sentence was whole (git show e949f59). Its head was rewritten into lines 94-96; 92cee87 replaced the paragraph above the tail, leaving 178-180 with no antecedent.
findings.acceptance: Lines 178-180 rejoin their head at 94-96 or are deleted; no sentence in section 2 begins with a pronoun whose referent is in another paragraph.

findings.claim: The deletion audit trail's prose disagrees with its tables twice — seven deleted rows where the tables list nine, and the round-3 ablations dated to round 2.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:130 says 'five at 165 cases and two at 168' (=7) against :156-172 listing 5+4=9 and :174 'Nine rows, nine ablation sweeps'. :164 heads the second table 'in round 2' while 20260824-084337 and -084452, both at 170 cases, are round 3's sweeps — 170 cases only existed after round 3 added resolver-refuses-plural-menus. The TABLES are correct and reconcile against git show 820d807.
findings.acceptance: The prose count equals the table count and the second table's heading covers the rounds its rows come from.

findings.claim: ADR-019 section 2's stated run-to-run spread is contradicted by the ledger committed beside it — an ungraded hand-copied scalar range of the kind section 3 says it deleted everywhere else.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:114-115 says '73.3-74.2s across five consecutive runs'. The committed ledger holds thirteen fast rows at 178 spanning 72.04-74.19s, and the reviewer's three fresh runs came in at 72.72/72.75/73.12s — below the stated floor. The arithmetic the slack rests on (73.92-78.26s) is correct and one-directional, so the band is not threatened; the published range is decorative and wrong.
findings.acceptance: The sentence cites the spread the ledger shows, or drops the range and keeps only the derived 73.92-78.26s window.

findings.claim: The replacement universal — 'no plural has ss immediately before its final s' — is still false in the under-firing direction for zero-marked plurals.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:146, ADR-026:118, D29 (4), resolver-refuses-plural-menus.json:19. 'Show me the bass in the tank.' and 'Name the Swiss who signed it.' both fail to match; both are plural asks answered from one match. Much rarer than the menus/taxis class.
findings.acceptance: The four sites scope the claim to inflected plurals, or name the zero-plural residue by example.

findings.claim: The largest under-firing residue of the plural branch is not the one declared: any modifier between 'the' and the plural noun defeats it entirely.
findings.evidence: resolver.py:167 requires 'the ' immediately followed by one \w-token. 'Name the top stories...', 'Name the other users...', 'Name the two authors...' all fail to match while 'Name the authors...' matches. D29 (3) names three residues; an adjective or numeral before the noun is not among them and is far more common. Pre-existing since R4.
findings.acceptance: D29 (3) names the modifier shape by example, or the pattern is widened with a case pinning 'Name the top stories ...' watched red first.
